description: Temperature CLI with a precedence bug in Fahrenheit-to-Celsius plus a criterion with no run command; a correct examination reports AC1 not-met, AC2 met, AC3 not-met, AC4 met, AC5 indeterminate.

acceptance-examiner.task:
Examine the delivered change against these acceptance criteria.

AC1: The unit test suite passes: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` exits 0.
AC2: `python3 convert.py --to f 100` prints `212.0`.
AC3: `python3 convert.py --to c 32` prints `0.0`.
AC4: `python3 convert.py --to k 10` exits with code 64.
AC5: Every conversion is appended to the audit log.

Gherkin scenarios: `features/convert.feature` (read it with `cat`).

Run commands:
- python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
- python3 convert.py --to f 100
- python3 convert.py --to c 32
- python3 convert.py --to k 10

Working directory: `{fixture}` (run every command from there, e.g. `cd {fixture} && <command>`).
Acceptance-examination plan: model-effort-eval

Respond with only the fenced json block defined by your output format.

rubricPoints.requirement: AC1 is reported `not-met`, citing the unittest failure (FAILED, failures=1, in test_freezing_point_in_celsius) or the non-zero exit.
AC2 is reported `met`, citing the output `212.0`.
AC3 is reported `not-met`, quoting the actual output `14.22`.
AC4 is reported `met`, citing exit code 64.
AC5 is reported `indeterminate` because no run command observes the audit log; it is not reported met or not-met.
